In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not yet have a robust estimate of the sub-stellar mass distribution.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UKIDSS LAS has been a successful survey for finding and characterising T dwarfs, and that the UKIDAS T dwarf sample will continue to grow as the survey progresses.
the T dwarf mass function is consistent with being a continuation of the M/L dwarf mass function, but that this result is not robust against systematic uncertainties.
T dwarfs in the LAS are not a complete sample (as expected) but are a good sample for statistical analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T dwarf sample from UKIDSS is now sufficiently large that it can be used to constrain the sub-stellar initial mass function.
the UKIDSS T dwarf discovery rate is now comparable to that of the 2MASS and SDSS surveys, despite being conducted at a higher limiting magnitude (J � 19).
